key_insight: Enforcing linear completeness in PIML removes a barrier to mesh-refinement convergence and enables rigorous H1- and L2-norm error estimates.
engineering_relevance: The approach accelerates substructure-based finite element analysis by learning reusable numerical shape functions while preserving conformity and convergence.
method: Learn material-distribution or element-geometry mappings to substructure shape functions with neural networks.
Bound numerical error using finite element discretization error and network generalization error.
Reconstruct transition-matrix columns under linear displacement constraints to reproduce linear polynomial fields.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments verify the theoretical results and demonstrate optimal convergence rates, good generalization performance, and numerical stability.
watch_item: Rigid-body displacement invariance alone does not guarantee convergence; implementation must enforce linear completeness, and error still depends on network generalization.
paper_title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
